title: Simple editor
use_when: Comments, notes and team updates. Headings, bold, italic, links, images and lists. This is the setup every new project starts with.

title: Comment box
use_when: Comments and short replies with links, lists and emoji, and a character limit.
notes: charCounterMax stops typing at 1,000 characters and shows a counter.

title: Blog post
use_when: Posts people publish, with headings, images, video and tables.
notes: Uploads need a server. Set imageUploadURL and videoUploadURL to endpoints that store the file and return { link }.

title: Business document
use_when: Letters and reports with fonts, page breaks, tracked changes and Word in and out.
notes: Export to Word files open in Microsoft Word. For other apps, convert the HTML to DOCX on your server.

title: Document editor
use_when: Long documents such as contracts and reports, edited on a page-like sheet.
notes: documentReady gives a page-like layout with settings suited to documents.

title: Advanced editor
use_when: A word processor in the browser with fonts, colors, tables, media and find and replace. This matches the toolbar on the Froala Demo page.

title: Every feature
use_when: Seeing the whole editor before you trim it. Loads every bundled plugin, with the toolbar in the order of the Froala website.
notes: This setup adds about 1.5 MB to your bundle. Trim it before you ship.
aiSupplementalTermsAccepted confirms that you accept the Froala AI terms. Read them before you ship.

title: Inline editing
use_when: Editing text in place on the page. The toolbar appears when text is selected.
notes: Attach the editor to the element you want to edit, such as a heading or a section of the page.

title: Markdown
use_when: People who prefer writing Markdown and want to see the formatted result next to it.
notes: To start in Markdown mode, call this.markdown.toggle() in the initialized event.

title: Headless editor
use_when: Your own toolbar and menus on the Froala editing engine. There is no Froala toolbar or popup.
notes: Your own controls call the editor API, for example editor.commands.bold(), editor.paragraphFormat.apply('H2'), editor.lists.format('UL'), editor.align.apply('center') and editor.link.insert(url, text).

title: Help desk reply
use_when: Support replies with the toolbar under the text, images and attachments.
notes: File uploads need a server. Set fileUploadURL to an endpoint that stores the file and returns { link }.

title: Track changes
use_when: Suggested edits that wait in the text and a side panel, where people accept or reject each one.
notes: Replace collabConfig.user with the signed-in user. Add realTime to collabConfig to share suggestions between people.

title: Admin form field
use_when: A compact field for admin forms that saves, reloads and validates like any other input.
notes: Read the value from the model. Validate its text, not its HTML, because an empty editor still holds markup.

title: Internal wiki
use_when: Team pages with headings, tables, code samples and links between pages.

title: Chat composer
use_when: A small composer for messages and tickets, with emoji and links.
notes: Read the message from the model or editor.html.get() when the user sends it, then clear it.

title: CMS article
use_when: Articles with headings, images, embeds and clean HTML for search.
notes: Set imageUploadURL before publishing, so images are stored on your server.

title: Markdown documentation
use_when: Documentation written in Markdown, with code blocks and tables.

title: Landing page blocks
use_when: Pages built from blocks you insert, drag and style.
notes: The Page builder whitepaper explains the approach. Find it with froala_find_presets and the query "page builder".

title: Newsroom
use_when: Several authors on one story, with comments, suggestions and versions.
notes: Real-time sharing needs a sync server. Read the collaborative plugin guide with froala_query_docs.

title: Course lesson
use_when: Lessons with video, tables, symbols and checklists. Equations come from the MathType plugin.
notes: For equations, follow the wiris example from froala_find_presets.
The Froala for LMS developers whitepaper has more detail. Find it with froala_find_presets and the query "LMS".

title: Quiz author
use_when: Questions with tables, symbols and a length limit.
notes: For equations, follow the wiris example from froala_find_presets.

title: Student writing
use_when: Essays and assignments with live word and character counts.
notes: For spell checking, follow the web-spell-checker example from froala_find_presets.

title: Offer letters and proposals
use_when: Offer letters, policies and proposals from reusable templates, with tables and page breaks.

title: Customer letters
use_when: Letters drafted from a template, reviewed with tracked changes and sent as Word files.

title: Contract review
use_when: Redlining a contract with tracked changes, starting from a Word file.

title: Support composer
use_when: Replies with signatures, personal fields and attachments.

title: CRM email
use_when: Sales emails with personal fields from your CRM records.
notes: useClasses set to false writes inline styles, which email clients need.

title: Newsletter
use_when: Campaign emails with layout tables and images.
notes: useClasses set to false writes inline styles, which email clients need.
Images in emails need public URLs. Set imageUploadURL to an endpoint that stores the image and returns its URL.
Check the result in the email clients your readers use before sending.

title: AI writing review
use_when: AI rewrites that arrive as suggestions your users accept or reject, on your own provider.
notes: Pass your model with aiAssistRequest or aiAssistEndpoint. The ai-assist examples from froala_find_presets show both.
aiSupplementalTermsAccepted confirms that you accept the Froala AI terms. Read them before you ship.

title: Moving from TinyMCE
use_when: Bringing TinyMCE content and settings across.
notes: Read the TinyMCE migration guide with froala_query_docs and the query "migrate from TinyMCE".

title: Moving from CKEditor
use_when: Bringing CKEditor 5 content and settings across.
notes: Read the CKEditor migration guide with froala_query_docs and the query "migrate from CKEditor".
